What is KIITEE Management?

KIITEE Management is a national-level computer-based entrance examination conducted by KIIT School of Management (KSOM) for admission to various MBA courses. The test is held across 16 cities in India. Candidates have to answer 150 questions in 150 minutes. The questions are asked from Quantitative Aptitude, Analytical Reasoning, General Knowledge and English. Candidates having CAT , MAT , CMAT and XAT scores are not required to appear for KIITEE Management exam .

The admission procedure of MBA at KIIT-SOM includes shortlisting of candidate on the basis of KIITEE-Management, Group Discussion (GD), Personal Interview (PI) and Writing Ability Test (WAT). The GD-PI and WAT rounds are conducted after the entrance exam result has been released. Candidates who clear KIITEE MBA entrance test, are eligible for the GD-PI and WAT. However, the selection will be made on the basis of every candidate’s academic record and KIITEE score.

MBA aspirants who have a valid score of CAT/MAT/XAT/CMAT/GMAT can also apply for KSOM MBA admission. Such candidates are not required to appear for KIITEE MBA and can directly participate in the GD-PI and WAT rounds upon selection.
KIITEE MBA exam syllabus includes Quantitative Aptitude, Analytical Reasoning, English and General Knowledge.

Quantitative Aptitude: Arithmetic, Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, Permutation & Combination, Probability, Logarithm, Simple & Compound Interest, Speed, Profit and Loss, Time and Distance, Percentage and Mensuration
Analytical Reasoning: Arrangements, Blood Relations, Coding-Decoding, Clocks and Calendars, Data Structures, Direction Sense, Puzzles and Series

English: Fill in the Blanks, Verbal Reasoning, Sentence Completion, Antonyms/Synonyms, Syllogisms, Jumbled Paragraphs, Para Completion and Inference, Contextual Usage, Foreign words used in English, Reading Comprehension, Analogies, Sentence Correction, One Word Substitution, Different Usage of Same Word and Idioms/Phrases
General Knowledge: Economics, Industries, Business, Advertising, International Trade, Politics, World Politics, Sports, Science, Arts and Entertainment etc.
Issues of Social Concern: Socio-economic and socio-political issues and rural and urban issues and development, etc.

The KIITEE MBA entrance exam is an institute specific entrance test. The score is accepted only by KIIT SOM for admission to its MBA Full Time and Super MBA courses. No other MBA institute accept KIITEE score for admission to post graduate programmes in management. So, those who wish to seek admission in any other B-School apart from KIIT SOM, must appear for the relevant MBA entrance exam as well. CAT, CMAT, XAT, MAT, ATMA. scores are also accepted for MBA admission at KIIT SOM.

Given below are key highlights of KIITEE Management exam for candidates to know before they proceed to read about it in detail.

The admission cut off will be announced by KIIT SOM at the time of WAT-GD-PI shortlisting. The difficulty level of KIITEE Management question paper is easy to moderate. Candidates can crack the exam with appropriate preparation of about three to four months. Those who have taken any national level test, can crack KIITEE MBA exam only by revision. The questions are asked from familiar topics, except in Issues of Social Concern. Even that section is not so difficult if one’s basic are in place. When preparing for KIITEE MBA, check out question papers of previous years to know what types of questions are asked. Solve them to assess your preparation level.

After the declaration of KIITEE MBA result, the institute will conduct Group Discussion (GD), Writing Ability Test (WAT) and Personal Interview (PI) to select candidates for MBA admission. The final selection will be based on candidate's performance in GD, WAT and PI. The institute will share the schedule of GD, WAT and PI with selected candidates.

Candidates who will clear the KIITEE MBA exam and meet the desired admission cut off, will be called by the institute to participate in the WAT-GD-PI. For selection of candidates, the admission panel will also take into consideration, academic record such as class 10, class 12 and graduation marks. However, maximum points will be for entrance exam score and WAT-GD-PI.
KIITEE Management Eligibility Criteria 2026
Given below are the main KIITEE Management eligibility criteria that candidates have to meet to appear in the exam:

value: The candidate must be a graduate in any discipline with 50 per cent aggregate marks from any university or possess an equivalent qualification recognized by the Ministry of HRD, Government of India.

The candidate must have 50 per cent aggregate marks (or equivalent CGPA) in the Class 10 and 12 examinations. Those who are awarded CGPA or grades in place of marks, their CGPA will be converted into equivalent marks based on the equivalence certified by the university/institution/board from where they obtained their degree/certificate. In absence of any instruction from the university, equivalence would be established by dividing obtained CGPA with the maximum CGPA and multiplying the fraction so obtained by 100.

Candidates appearing for the final examination for the Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent examination) are eligible to apply. However, they have to clear their final exam of Bachelor’s degree by June 30, 2026.
Foreign/NRI candidates with same academic qualification will be considered for admission process on the basis of their valid GMAT scores. Application fee for them is USD 500.
Domestic candidates who possess valid scores of CAT, XAT, CMAT, MAT will be directly eligible for KSOM MBA Group Discussion and Personal Interview.

blocks.value: No, you can’t apply for KIITEE MBA. KIIT SOM has the eligibility criteria of minimum 50 per cent in graduation for all candidates. There is no marks relaxation for Reserved category candidates either. The minimum score criterion is fixed by the AICTE for full-time MBA degree programmes for all colleges in India, which the institutes have to follow. Thus, those planning to purse MBA must score a minimum of 50 per cent in graduation.

Even if you are applying while still in graduation, you need to have an aggregate of 50 per cent in the first two years of the degree course. If you do not have the minimum score required, your application form will be rejected.

KIITEE Management exam is conducted in online or computer based test mode at designated examination centres in 15 cities across India. The exam centres are allotted to candidates as per their choice of city. Candidates have to mention their preferred city for allotment of test centre in the KIITEE MBA application form.

In a computer based test, each candidate is allotted a computer system. They have to log into KIITEE MBA dashboard to access the test. They can read the question on screen and use the computer mouse to choose the correct answer from the options given under every question.

Candidates have to complete marking the correct answers within the stipulated time. There will be an onscreen camera indicating time left for the test window to close. Once the test window closes, candidates cannot make any entry.

To appear for KIITEE MBA exam, a candidate needs to have completed graduation or equivalent with a minimum of 50 per cent aggregate or equivalent. The minimum score qualification of 50 per cent applies to Reserved category candidates too. The graduation degree can be in any stream but must be from a recognised university.

Students who are in their final year of bachelor’s degree course are also eligible to appear in the KIITEE MBA exam. Final year students are also eligible to apply. However, they will have to ensure that their aggregate in the first two years in above 50 per cent and the final year scores (when announced) is also above 50 per cent. Until they submit their final year graduation result, their admission to KSOM will remain provisional.

KIITEE Management 2026 admission process will consist of four stages - application,  entrance test, result and GD/PI. Check below important points related to each stage.
KIITEE Management 2026 Application process

KIITEE Management 2026 registration process is online. Aspirants can apply online by paying INR 1,500 via debit/credit card or netbanking, as exam fee. KIITEE MBA application form is to be submitted in online mode only.

The admit card for KIITEE Management 2026 exam can be downloaded by using login credentials. Admit card is a mandatory document to be carried to the exam hall, hence the candidates must download and take a print out of the same.

KIITEE Management 2026

KIITEE Management test is held at 16 test centres across the country. Candidates have to take the test on s computer system. The question paper contains MCQs from Quantitative Aptitude, GK, English, Analytical Reasoning and Issue of Social Concern.
KIITEE Management 2026 Result

KITTEE Management result is released on the official website. Candidates can download their scorecards from the official website by using their index number and date of birth. The scorecard contains candidates scores and other details required in GD/PI. Qualifying candidates will be eligible for selection round, i.e. GD/PI.

KIIT GD/PI

Candidates successful in KIITEE Management exam will be shortlisted for GD/PI round. Candidates who shall have applied through CAT/XAT/CMAT/MAT/GMAT scores will also be shortlisted for this round. They selected candidates will have to be present in person during GD/PI. Final admission will be granted on the basis of the candidate’s overall performance in the test, GD/PI and academics. Candidates can apply for KIITEE Management exam 2026 , in two modes, when the dates are declared.

So as soon as the KIITEE admit card is released, candidates must check the test city and test centre details. In order to avoid any confusion, they must visit the centre at least once before the exam day.

1. Reach exam centre as per reporting time mentioned on your admit card.
2. Carry two copies of admit card, one photo ID card, passport size photos
3. PwD candidates should carry relevant certificates and documents
4. Carry a blue/black ball point pen for signing attendance sheet
Exam day don'ts:
1. Don't carry items electronic items
2. Don't wear closed shoes, jewellery made of metal, jackets, clothes with pockets, mehendi on palms.
4. Don't be late for exam. The entry gates will be closed 15 minutes before start time.
KIITEE MBA Syllabus

The syllabus of KIITEE Management exam is similar to other MBA entrance exams. KIIT Management syllabus 2026 includes Quantitative Aptitude, Analytical Reasoning, English, General Knowledge. It has an additional subject called Issue of Social Concern. Check below subjects included in KIITEE Management syllabus 2026 and their weightage.

The KIITEE MBA syllabus is prescribed by KIIT School of Management. The syllabus of the exam is similar to other MBA entrance exams such as CAT, MAT, XAT, CMAT, ATMA. The exam is a speed-based test designed to assess the candidate's business aptitude, reasoning skill, mathematical ability and communication skills. Since, MBA is a programme designed to produce skilled managers in various domains, the syllabus of entrance for the same is designed in a way that it allows the B-school to ascertain whether the aspirant has the flair and ability to perform tasks which will require them to use analytical ability, logical reasoning, data interpretation and English communication.

In the Issue of Social concern section of KIITEE MBA, questions will be asked from topics such as government schemes, socio-political events, social issues, Indian economy and its impact on social groups, social change and reformation, etc. This is a unique section of KIITEE MBA and no other entrance exam has any such section. To prepare for Issue of Social Concern section of the KIITEE MBA, candidates must check the previous year question papers. The questions of past year will help them understand the topics from which questions are usually asked and what are the types of answers expected. If you understand the gist of the give situation (issue), you will be able to answer the questions easily.

About six months will be more than enough to prepare for KIITEE MBA exam as the syllabus is same as other MBA entrance exams. Candidates can refer to books and study material of CAT exam to prepare for KIITEE Management exam. They need to devote 4-5 hours daily to exam preparation and practice sample papers of KIITEE MBA. Key topics to study are as follows:

Quantitative Aptitude: Arithmetic, Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, Probability, Mensuration, Permutation & Combination, Simple & Compound Interest, Speed Time and Distance, Profit and Loss, Percentage and Logarithm, etc.
Analytical Reasoning: Arrangements, Coding-Decoding, Data Structures, Puzzles, Blood Relations, Clocks and Calendars, Direction, Series, etc.

English: Fill in the Blanks, Verbal Reasoning, Sentence Completion, Antonyms/Synonyms, Syllogisms, Jumbled Paragraphs, Para Completion, Reading Comprehension, Foreign words, Sentence Correction, Idioms/Phrases, One Word Substitution, etc.
General Knowledge: Economics, Industries, Business, Advertising, International Trade, Politics, World Politics, Sports, Science and Arts and Entertainment

Time duration is two and a half hours or 150 minutes without sectional time limit and break.
The KIITEE Management question paper will have 150 questions
The format of questions is “Objective-type" questions answers

Study materials of Quantitative Aptitude, Analytical Reasoning, English and General Knowledge are easily available so there are no challenges. Candidates must focus more on the fifth section - Issue of Social Concern - during preparation as not much study material is available for the same.
